document.abstract: The results of subjective rankings of various speech and music selections containing various amounts and types of flutter are presented. These rankings are compared to the type of flutter and the results of flutter measurements using peak and rms indications and various flutter-rate weighting networks. The comparisons show that a meter using an rms indicating device and a flutter-rate weighting network will provide flutter measurements which are directly related to the obnoxious quality that the flutter imparts to music and speech.
